tools.name: check_tx
tools.description: Run on every transaction before signing. Shows what each wallet gains and loses, blocks drainer tricks, and catches failures and expired blockhashes before you pay a fee. Decodes each step, dry-runs it on live mainnet, finds each wallet's SOL and token changes, and answers OK, REVIEW or BLOCK with r

tools.name: tx_matches
tools.description: Run just before signing a transfer built from a request like "send 5 USDC to X", or a swap built for "swap 1 USDC for JUP". tools.name: explain_tx
tools.description: Run after a transaction lands or fails, to report what happened instead of guessing from logs. For failures it names the failing program and the fix. tools.name: fee
tools.description: Run before setting a priority fee. Gives the price in the unit Compute Budget expects (micro-lamports per compute unit) and the total in SOL, so a unit mix-up never overpays. tools.name: tx_version
tools.description: Run when code can't find or read a transaction that is on chain, or before relying on code that reads other people's transactions. tools.name: build_tx
tools.description: Run when an agent needs to send SOL or a token, or swap through Jupiter: it returns the unsigned transaction already checked, with ready_to_sign and the reasons. Sign only when ready_to_sign is true. Builds a SOL or token transfer, or a Jupiter swap, as an unsigned transaction with a fresh blockhash

tools.name: find_token
tools.description: Run whenever a user names a token ("buy BONK"). Tickers aren't unique; copycats reuse them. Never take an address from memory. Finds the real address for a ticker or name, ranks matches by verification and liquidity, and warns when copycats share the ticker. Example: {"name": "BONK"}. Cost: 25 free

tools.name: token_safety
tools.description: Run before buying, accepting or recommending a token. Answers SAFE, CAUTION or AVOID with exact reasons from chain and market data, plus rug_chance (high, with reasons, or null). Simulates a real holder selling, then checks if liquidity can be pulled, the creator's record, insider wallet networks, i

tools.name: token_traders
tools.description: Run to see who bought a token early and who profited: launch-block snipers, the pool creator, wallets that sold more than they bought (got tokens some other way), and ordinary traders. Reads a token's pool from its first transaction for a set time and lists the wallets that traded it: buys, sells, S

tools.name: wallet
tools.description: Run when asked what a wallet holds or is worth. One call instead of balance + tokens + history; spam is left out of the total. SOL balance, top tokens with USD values, estimated total, and recent activity in one answer. Example: {"wallet": "<address>"}. Cost: 25 free calls a day, then $0.01 USDC per

tools.name: trace
tools.description: Run when a wallet was drained or money went missing, or before trusting an address someone gave you: follows the money and flags sweeper, pass-through and lookalike-address patterns. Follows a wallet's money through its recent transactions: net SOL and token change and the other side of each, where

tools.name: balance
tools.description: Run before sending SOL or paying fees, to confirm the wallet has enough. Never trust a remembered balance. A wallet's SOL balance, read from the chain. Example: {"wallet": "<address>"}. Cost: 25 free calls a day, then $0.01 USDC per call (x402). Outputs explained: GET /api/tools/balance.

tools.name: tokens
tools.description: Run to learn which tokens a wallet holds and how much. Ranked by USD value; unverified (often spam airdrop) tokens are flagged so you don't report fake holdings. tools.description: Run to see a wallet's recent activity or get a real transaction ID. Never make one up. Lists a wallet's latest transactions, newest first, whether each worked, and a plain error name for failures. Example: {"wallet": "<address>", "how_many": 5}. tools.name: blockhash
tools.description: Run just before building a transaction to sign. Blockhashes expire in about 60-90 seconds; this says how long is left. tools.name: token_account
tools.description: Run before sending a token. Tokens go to the recipient's token account, not their wallet, and models can't work that address out. Finds the token account (ATA) for a wallet and token with the token's real program, says if it exists, and prices creating it. Example: {"wallet": "<recipient>", "token":

tools.name: whats_this
tools.description: Run when unsure what an address is, before sending to it or passing it on. SOL sent to a token or program address can be lost for good. Says what any address is (wallet, token account, token, program, stake account and more) with its key facts. Example: {"address": "EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wE

tools.name: convert
tools.description: Run before putting any token amount in a transaction. "5 USDC" is 5,000,000 raw units; wrong decimals send 1,000x too much or too little. Converts between normal amounts and raw units with the token's real on-chain decimals. Example: {"token": "SOL", "amount": "0.5"} gives 500000000. Cost: 25 free c

tools.name: why_failed
tools.description: Run whenever a Solana transaction or dry run fails, before retrying. Retrying blind burns fees. Turns a Solana error (hex code, log line or RPC error) into the plain cause and fix. Offline, no chain call. Example: {"error": "custom program error: 0x1771", "program": "JUP6LkbZbjS1jKKwapdHNy74zcZ3tLUZ

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_tx · Private data: check_tx, tx_matches, explain_tx, build_tx, find_token, token_safety, token_traders, wallet, trace, balance, tokens, history, token_account, whats_this, convert · Public sink: tx_matches, build_tx, find_token, convert · Destructive: check_tx, tx_matches, explain_tx, fee, tx_version, build_tx, find_token, token_safety, token_traders, wallet, trace, balance, tokens, history, blockhash, token_account, whats_this, convert, why_failed.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_tx · Private data: check_tx, tx_matches, explain_tx, build_tx, find_token, token_safety, token_traders, wallet, trace, balance, tokens, history, token_account, whats_this, convert · Public sink: tx_matches, build_tx, find_token, convert · Destructive: check_tx, tx_matches, explain_tx, fee, tx_version, build_tx, find_token, token_safety, token_traders, wallet, trace, balance, tokens, history, blockhash, token_account, whats_this, convert, why_failed

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
